title: Collapse of the $p$-th moment along the last coordinate
statement:
Let $p > 0$ and let $f : \{0,1\}^{n+1} \to \bbr$ be a Boolean function of arity $n+1$. Writing $(x', b) \in \{0,1\}^n \times \{0,1\}$ for the point of $\{0,1\}^{n+1}$ whose first $n$ coordinates are $x'$ and whose last coordinate is $b$, one has
\[
  \E\bigl[\,\abs{f}^p\,\bigr]
  \;=\;
  \E_{x' \in \{0,1\}^n}\!\left[\tfrac12\Bigl(\abs{f(x', 0)}^p + \abs{f(x', 1)}^p\Bigr)\right],
\]
where both expectations are taken with respect to the uniform measure on the respective hypercubes.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued Boolean function of arity $n+1$
